  "evidence_ids": [
    "E1.1",
    "E1.2"
  ],
  "reasons": [
    "Total profit is Rs. 1,50,000 divided in ratio 3:2:1, giving P = Rs. 75,000, Q = Rs. 50,000, and R = Rs. 25,000.",
    "R's shortfall against the guaranteed Rs. 30,000 is Rs. 5,000, borne by P and Q in ratio 3:2.",
    "P bears 3/5 of Rs. 5,000 = Rs. 3,000, leaving P with Rs. 75,000 - Rs. 3,000 = Rs. 72,000."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Profit & Loss Appropriation Account",
  "syllabus_topic": "Guarantee of profit to a partner",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "The firm's profit of Rs. 1,50,000 is divisible among P, Q, and R in the ratio 3:2:1.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "R is guaranteed a minimum profit of Rs. 30,000.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "Shortfall in R's guaranteed profit is borne by P and Q in the ratio 3:2.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "B",
      "strongest_reading": "P gets Rs. 75,000 if P does not bear any deficiency towards R's guarantee.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "P gets Rs. 73,000 if P bears only Rs. 2,000 instead of 3/5 of Rs. 5,000.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "P gets Rs. 70,000 if P bears the entire deficiency of Rs. 5,000 individually.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "blocking_defects": [],
  "style_notes": [],
  "cuet_fit": {
    "criteria": {
      "syllabus_objective": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Directly tests computation of partner profit shares under minimum profit guarantee."
      },
      "format_authenticity": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Standard single-response numerical MCQ formatted identically to CUET Accountancy questions."
      },
      "level_calibration": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Requires two-step arithmetic typical of Class 12 partnership accounting exam items."
      },
      "discrimination_value": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Distractors isolate unadjusted profit (B), swapped shortfall ratio (C), and full deficiency borne (D)."
      }
    },
    "reasoning_steps": 3,
    "estimated_difficulty": "medium",
    "cognitive_level": "application",
    "exemplar_ids_compared": []
  },
  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "arithmetic",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "The firm's profit for the year is Rs. 1,50,000 and the profit sharing ratio of P, Q and R is 3:2:1.",
      "reason": "P's gross share Rs. 75,000 minus P's 3/5 deficiency share Rs. 3,000 equals Rs. 72,000."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Rs. 75,000",
      "premise_source": "arithmetic",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "The guarantee is given by P and Q, who will bear any shortfall in the ratio 3:2.",
      "reason": "Rs. 75,000 fails to deduct P's Rs. 3,000 contribution to R's Rs. 5,000 shortfall."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Rs. 73,000",
      "premise_source": "arithmetic",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "bear any shortfall in the ratio 3:2.",
      "reason": "Rs. 73,000 results from deducting Rs. 2,000 (Q's share of deficiency) instead of Rs. 3,000."
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Rs. 70,000",
      "premise_source": "arithmetic",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "The guarantee is given by P and Q, who will bear any shortfall in the ratio 3:2.",
      "reason": "Rs. 70,000 wrongly assumes P bears the whole Rs. 5,000 deficiency."
    }
  ]
}
